title: The share of US job ads that mention AI has nearly tripled since 2025
description: Share of US job postings mentioning AI, monthly 2019 to 2026, from Indeed Hiring Lab data: 2.74% in January 2025, 7.60% now.
dek: In October 2026, 7.60% of US job postings on Indeed mentioned AI, up from 2.74% in January 2025 and the highest share since the series began in 2019.
findings: The share rose from 2.74% in January 2025 to 7.60% in October 2026, about 2.8 times as high in 21 months. It went up in 20 of those 21 month-to-month steps.

This is not the first AI hiring wave. The share hit 3.23% in March 2022, then fell to 1.71% by June 2023. The fall ran straight through ChatGPT's launch in November 2022, so the launch did not stop a fall already under way in tech hiring.

In October 2026 the US (7.60%) trailed Ireland (15.23%) and the UK (10.23%). Canada showed 19.93%, but much of that comes from an Ontario law, in force since January 2026, that makes employers say when AI screens applicants.

On Hacker News's monthly 'Who is hiring?' thread, where startups post, the AI share is far higher: 51.6% of postings in November 2026. The two counts use different word lists, so compare their direction, not their levels: both climb.

chart.subtitle: Monthly average of Indeed's daily share (7-day trailing average), January 2019 to October 2026
chart.creditSource: Indeed Hiring Lab AI Tracker (CC BY 4.0)

method: Indeed Hiring Lab publishes, for each day, the share of job postings on Indeed whose text includes AI terms such as 'machine learning', 'data science', 'artificial intelligence', 'generative AI' and 'large language models'. Each daily figure is a 7-day trailing average.
I averaged the daily US figures into calendar months, January 2019 to October 2026. The newest month in the data is October 2026.
The data counts postings that mention AI anywhere, including company descriptions. It is not a count of AI jobs. One posting can say 'we use AI to screen applicants' and still count.

The data and Hiring Lab's method are free to reuse under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, with credit to Indeed Hiring Lab. The chart and monthly averages here are my own calculation from it.
